subject: Clarifying invoice consolidation & seller-fee pass-through for Contoso listing across cloud marketplaces
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@amazon.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@cloudbridge.io
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Seller fee / invoice path questions for Contoso (AWS marketplace)

Hi Vivek,

Quick one from our settlements team while we finalize the Contoso listing: Contoso’s finance team is asking for clarification on how marketplace fees will appear on invoices and whether they should expect a single consolidated invoice or separate vendor settlement statements. A few specifics they raised: 

- Will Contoso receive a single invoice that includes the gross charge and an "AWS fee" line (so they can claim the full SaaS cost), or will they get an AWS invoice + a separate settlement/credit from the marketplace?
- For US customers, do you need a W-9 from Contoso for our remittance/1099 purposes?
- For EU customers (not in this thread, but FYI) we sometimes see reverse-charge VAT implications – any documentation you can provide on how Redwood prefers to handle VAT passthrough would be helpful.

Attaching the AWS Marketplace settlement guide we typically share. If you can map what Redwood expects vs what AWS will do, that will speed up Contoso’s procurement.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Marketplace Partnerships – AWS
Attachment: Marketplace_Settlement_Guide.pdf

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@amazon.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Seller fee / invoice path questions for Contoso (AWS marketplace)

Sarah —

Thanks for the note and the attachment. Looping in Vanessa (Billing Ops) and Laura (Marketplaces PM) so we can give Contoso a clear, actionable mapping. High level we need: 

- A short diagram (one-pager) that shows AWS invoice -> customer / AWS settlement -> Redwood payout sequence and where fees are deducted. That helps us determine whether we should expect to issue a credit memo or a consolidated invoice.
- Confirmation on whether AWS will include an "AWS marketplace fee" line on the customer-facing invoice or if that is only on the settlement statement (we see this vary).
- Any standard language AWS prefers for tax/VAT handling notes in the invoice footer (especially for EU reverse-charge scenarios).

I've drafted a Redwood note (attached) describing our three preferred flows. We’ll turn that into a recommended approach for Contoso once we understand what AWS will actually send them.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachment: RDW_marketplace_tax_notes_2026-05.pdf

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@amazon.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Seller fee / invoice path questions for Contoso (AWS marketplace)

Sarah / team —

Quick operational context from billing: in our experience there are two common marketplace patterns and the tax treatment differs materially between them. Short checklist below and two follow ups we need from AWS to finalize for Contoso.

Checklist (what we need):
- Who is the invoice originator to the end-customer (AWS vs Redwood)?
- Will AWS include a visible marketplace fee line on the customer invoice, or only in the settlement statement to Redwood?
- Which legal entity will be used for the settlement (US vs EU entity)? This drives withholding, 1099/W-9 handling.

Operational note: if AWS invoices the customer and pays Redwood net of fees, Contoso will often end up with an AWS invoice (showing the full charge) plus a separate settlement report. That can create confusion when customers try to reclaim VAT or reconcile spend. For US customers a completed W-9 from Contoso is sufficient for our payout records. For cross-border EU cases we need clear VAT evidence (VAT ID + applicable reverse-charge confirmation).

Action items for AWS:
1) Provide the standard customer invoice sample for listings where AWS is the invoice originator (showing whether marketplace fee appears).
2) Confirm settlement entity and remittance schedule.

I attached an example settlement CSV from a prior customer and a short one-page checklist we send to customers requesting W-9/ VAT evidence. Also attaching a short template we use to request W-9 from Contoso.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Billing Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Settlement_example.csv, Contoso_W9_requested.docx

From: Contoso AR <ar@contoso.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Seller fee / invoice path questions for Contoso (AWS marketplace)

Hi Vanessa / Vivek —

Thanks for the clarity so far. We did receive an invoice from AWS and a separate settlement statement referencing Redwood; that’s what prompted our team to reach out. A couple things on our end: 

- We attached our completed W-9 (Contoso_W9.pdf) — please confirm receipt and whether you need anything else for US tax records.
- To avoid double-counting fees for VAT/expense purposes, can Redwood either issue a single consolidated invoice or provide a credit memo for the AWS marketplace fee line? Our AP team prefers one supplier invoice where possible.
- What’s the expected timeline to reconcile the AWS settlement and issue any required credit/adjustment? We are trying to close our month end by 31 May.

Appreciate a short plan so we can coordinate with AWS if needed.

Best,
Marta Reyes
Head of Accounts Payable | Contoso Technologies
Attachment: Contoso_W9.pdf

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marta Reyes <ar@contoso.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@amazon.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Seller fee / invoice path questions for Contoso (AWS marketplace)

Marta / Sarah —

Thanks for the W-9 and the heads-up on month end. Based on the information so far, recommended path and timeline below. I listed alternatives in case AWS cannot change the invoice originator behavior.

Recommended (preferred) — Option A:
- Redwood acts as the invoice originator for Contoso (single supplier invoice). We will: issue a single monthly invoice to Contoso showing gross product charges and a separate line in the invoice PDF called "Marketplace fee (AWS) - informational" with zero net tax impact. Separately we will provide the AWS settlement statement for accounting reconciliation. 
- Benefits: single supplier invoice for AP, clearer expense reclaim for customers, faster month-end close.
- Timeline: if AWS can provide a settlement statement template by EOD Friday (30 May) we can issue a consolidated invoice and supporting settlement file by 02 June.

Alternative — Option B:
- AWS remains invoice originator. Contoso receives AWS invoice, Redwood receives settlement net of fees. We will: issue a credit memo / supplier invoice to Contoso that reflects Redwood’s revenue net of AWS fee so Contoso has a single supplier document for expense purposes. This requires coordination with AWS to ensure the fee is visible on the settlement so we can match values.
- Timeline: depends on AWS settlement timing; target to reconcile within 7 business days after settlement posts.

Next steps (immediate):
1) Sarah: can you confirm whether AWS can (a) provide the settlement statement sample and (b) whether the AWS customer-facing invoice can include an informative marketplace fee line?
2) Vanessa / Marcus: once we confirm, prepare the invoice template and credit memo flow. Marcus — please flag any 1099/US tax implications if Redwood acts as originator.
3) Marta: we received Contoso_W9.pdf — will confirm ingestion to our AR system and notify you if anything else is needed.

If everyone is aligned I’ll draft a short addendum we can DocuSign with Contoso (simple one paragraph) describing the invoice format and reconciliation cadence.

Best,
— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | www.redwood.ai
